task_family: iid tabular binary classification (mixed categorical/ordinal survey features, hard-label metric)

test_window.evidence: No date/time column in any file (20 train cols / 19 test cols, all demographic-lifestyle survey fields). id is a contiguous row counter: train 0..140699, test 140700..234499 — a sequential split of one generated table, not a temporal boundary. Per-column null rates match almost exactly across train/test (Academic Pressure 0.8017 vs 0.7999, Work Pressure 0.1984 vs 0.2002, Profession 0.2603 vs 0.2626), and categorical vocabularies coincide — consistent with a random iid split of a single synthetic population.

split_policy.scheme: StratifiedKFold on Depression (5-fold), shuffled, fixed seed
forbidden: unstratified plain KFold — 18.17% positive rate plus an accuracy metric makes per-fold prevalence drift directly move the tuned threshold
time-based / TimeSeriesSplit — no time axis exists; would only shrink the training set
any target/frequency encoding fit outside the fold (City 98, Degree 115, Profession 64, Name 422 levels are the tempting targets)
split_policy.group_key: none — no repeated-entity column. Name (422 distinct first names over 140,700 rows) is a synthetic attribute, not a person identifier, so it is a categorical feature and not a grouping key.

metric.name: accuracy
traps: hard 0/1 submission (sample_submission has integer labels) — every model must emit a decision, so the threshold is part of the model and must be picked on OOF, never on train predictions

majority-class floor is 0.8183 (all-zeros); real headroom sits in a narrow band above it, so CV deltas are small and fold noise can dominate — compare candidates on identical folds and prefer repeated-seed CV before accepting a small win

accuracy is threshold-sensitive but calibration-insensitive: probability calibration is worthless on its own, whereas any reweighting (is_unbalance / scale_pos_weight) shifts the optimal threshold away from 0.50 and must be re-tuned jointly
threshold optimization is known in this repo to transfer poorly from CV to LB on binary tasks — tune it, but bound the search and prefer a flat-optimum plateau over a spiky argmax

external_data.reason: config.yaml special_rules sets external_data_allowed: false, internet_access_allowed: false, pretrained_models_allowed: false. Independently of rules, the target has no country/date/geography axis on which a whitelisted macro or calendar source could join — City is an unkeyed Indian-city string with no time dimension, so no whitelist row (World Bank, holidays, ISO, ECB, OWID) has a usable join key here.

data_level: Canonicalize dirty free-text ordinals before encoding: Sleep Duration has 36 raw levels but 4 carry 99.98% of rows ('Less than 5 hours', '5-6 hours', '7-8 hours', 'More than 8 hours'); map those to an ordered numeric scale and bucket the long tail as 'other'. Dietary Habits has 23 levels over a real 3-level ordinal (Healthy/Moderate/Unhealthy) plus junk ('Yes', 'No', 'More Healthy', 2 rows each).

Treat missingness as structural role signal, not noise: Academic Pressure / CGPA / Study Satisfaction are null for ~80% of rows (the Working Professionals) and Work Pressure / Job Satisfaction for ~20% (the Students). Emit explicit is_student / is_professional flags and keep NaN as an informative value (GBDT native NaN handling) rather than imputing.

Collapse the two disjoint blocks into shared axes: pressure = coalesce(Academic Pressure, Work Pressure) and satisfaction = coalesce(Study Satisfaction, Job Satisfaction), each paired with its source-block flag. Both sub-columns are 1-5 ordinals with near-identical marginals (means 3.14/3.00 and 2.95/2.97), so a merged column doubles the per-level sample count while the flag preserves separability.

High-cardinality categoricals (City 98, Degree 115, Profession 64, Name 422) — pass as native GBDT categoricals first. If target encoding is tried, fit strictly inside the fold; the prior-season feature set here used label encoding only and is therefore fold-safe as a comparison baseline.

Ordinal-aware numeric treatment for the 1-5 Likert fields (Financial Stress, pressure, satisfaction) and for Work/Study Hours (0-12, 13 levels) — keep raw ordinal plus a few crosses with the role flag rather than one-hot.

Interaction candidates grounded in the domain rather than search: suicidal-thoughts flag x age band, pressure x satisfaction, Work/Study Hours x role, Financial Stress x role. 'Have you ever had suicidal thoughts ?' is near-balanced (50.6% No) and is the single most likely dominant predictor.
model_level: GBDT with native categorical handling as the primary family (LightGBM/CatBoost) — matches TASK-CAT-ONLY, where encoding choice is the dominant lever.
Optimize the decision threshold on out-of-fold probabilities inside the metric function, so every blend candidate is scored post-threshold rather than on rank.

Class weighting (is_unbalance / scale_pos_weight) is optional at 18% positives; if used, re-tune the threshold jointly — the prior-season run needed 0.75 after enabling is_unbalance, which is a symptom of reweighting, not of the data.
Blend on hard-label accuracy via majority vote or threshold-after-averaging probabilities; averaging probabilities then thresholding once is the better default because voting discards margin.
TASK-BLEND-DECOR: once the pool is deep GBDT-dominated, add one shallow heavily-regularized member from a different library as a decorrelator before re-optimizing weights.

considered_and_rejected_priors.reason: no date column and no forecasting language; test is an iid row split
no daily series, no store/product keys
18 features over 140,700 rows — rows greatly exceed columns
single scalar binary output, no generative grid/sequence structure
metric is accuracy, not an MAE/SMAPE/quantile family member

trigger is positive rate <= ~2%; actual rate is 18.17%. The prior's 'beware accuracy-style thresholds' caution is still carried into metric.traps, but the resampling/stratification prescription is not invoked as a match.
